rules.title: {name} is the host of every video.
rules.body: {name} appears in about half of all scenes, talking to camera and doing what the narration describes; the other half are people-free key visuals. {name} is index 0 in the roster.

rules.title: {name}'s identity is locked.
rules.body: In every scene of every video {name} keeps the same face, hair, facial hair, eye colour, skin tone, build and marks: {invariants}. Only clothing and setting vary.

rules.title: {name}'s locked features are written into every prompt.
rules.body: Every prompt that draws {name} carries the locked feature list ({invariants}) verbatim; nothing about {name}'s look is left for the model to decide.

rules.title: {name} is described in positive, concrete terms — never negations.
rules.body: Say what {name} HAS, never what {name} lacks; a negation summons the thing it names.

rules.title: {name} dresses as a {role}: {attire}.
rules.body: {name}'s wardrobe stays inside '{attire}' — one outfit per act, chosen once per render, never per-scene randomness, never a costume that contradicts the role.

rules.title: Never two of {name} in one frame.
rules.body: One {name} per scene — never a copy in the background, in a crowd, on a poster or on a device screen.

rules.title: {name}'s name is never printed in the video.
rules.body: No chart heading, document, sign, badge or screen shows the text '{name}'. Props are people-free or use generic printed content.

rules.title: {name} resembles no other character.
rules.body: Extras and other roster characters must not share {name}'s face, hair or silhouette; {name} is unique to this owner's Style and is never reused as a system asset.

rules.title: {name} speaks with one locked voice.
rules.body: Every video narrated by {name} uses the same voice, tuned once in the Voice Tuner; a different voice is a deliberate per-video choice by the owner.

rules.title: {name} works with the channel's key props.
rules.body: When {name} is on screen doing something, it is something a {role} does: reading a statement, pointing at a chart, holding a card — never filler poses (pointing at nothing, peace signs, staring at a calendar).
